messages.subject: Warning that solution not found with results
parts:
Hello, 

I've attached an .RData object that contains the R objects necessary to run the code below. The model is producing a warning that a solution has not been found, but the code is also still producing point estimates and standard errors and indicates that the model converged normally after 247 iterations. I've never seen this behavior in lavaan before (in my past experience a warning to this effect would not produce any results) and I'm just wondering how to interpret that?

Thanks very much!
 -Andrew 

load("WarningExample.RData")
require(lavaan)
Model1_Results <- sem(Model1, sample.cov = S_LD, estimator = "DWLS", WLS.V = W_Reorder, sample.nobs = 2,std.lv=TRUE)

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Warning that solution not found with results
parts:
Indeed, this is confusing. This is 'new' in 0.6-7: if the first attempt
to estimate the parameters fails, lavaan tries again. In fact, 4
attempts are done (2 different starting values, 2 different ways to
handle the scale of the data). In your case, the first two attempts
failed, producing two warnings, but the third one succeeded.

So you can ignore the warnings. In a future update, they will no longer
be shown (if one of the attempts succeeded).

In your setting, the initial starting values did not work. But the
'simple' ones do work:

fit <- sem(Model1, sample.cov = S_LD, estimator = "DWLS", WLS.V =
W_Reorder, sample.nobs = 2,std.lv=TRUE, verbose = TRUE, start = "simple")

producing no warning.

Yves.
